ك.ف.ر.why: The CAMeL MSA lexicon glosses kafara only in modern senses (blaspheme, renege Islam, atone). In the Quran it means to disbelieve or deny, and also to be ungrateful (e.g. 2:152, 14:7). Added 2026-11-03. كُفْر: the lexicon glosses the noun only as 'infidelity; atheism'. In the Quran it is disbelief (ٱلْكُفْرَ بِٱلْإِيمَٰنِ 2:108). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 3).

#.ت.#.why: The lexicon reads the Form IV imperative آتِ (give!) only as the noun 'coming'; it glosses the verb آتَى as 'give; offer' elsewhere, so 'give' is attested for this root. Quranic use: 2:201, 17:26. Added 2026-11-03. CAMeL writes this root with its weak radicals as #.ت.#.

#.ل.#.why: The lexicon glosses tawallā only as 'take charge of; be in charge of'. In the Quran its most frequent sense is to turn away (تَوَلَّى عَنْ), e.g. 37:90, 37:174, 80:1. Added 2026-11-03. CAMeL writes this root (و.ل.ي) with its weak radicals as #.ل.#. Also: وَلِيّ: the lexicon glosses it only as 'successor; heir; patron'. In the Quran a وَلِيّ is a guardian or protector (2:257, 4:45), as in MSA وَلِيُّ الْأَمْرِ, a child's guardian. Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 2).

#.ح.#.why: The lexicon glosses awḥā as 'inspire; suggest' only. In the Quran it is the verb of divine revelation (وَحْي), e.g. 42:3, 53:4. Added 2026-11-03. CAMeL writes this root (و.ح.ي) as #.ح.#.

ل.ق.#.why: The lexicon reads the Form IV imperative أَلْقِ (throw!) only as 'shine' (root أ.ل.ق) or 'meet'; it glosses the verb أَلْقَى as 'deliver; throw' elsewhere, so 'throw' is attested for this root. Quranic use: 20:19, 20:69. Added 2026-11-03. CAMeL writes this root (ل.ق.ي) as ل.ق.#.

ح.ب.ب.why: The lexicon reads the Form IV imperative أَحْبِبْ (love!) only as the first person 'I endear'; it glosses the verb أَحَبَّ as 'love; like' elsewhere, so 'love' is attested for this root. Added 2026-11-03.

ر.ز.ق.why: The lexicon glosses razaqa only as 'bestow; endow' (and the passive 'be bestowed'). In the Quran it is the verb of God providing sustenance, e.g. 2:3, 42:19, 51:58; 'provide' is the standard rendering. Added 2026-11-03.

ع.ق.ل.why: The lexicon glosses ʿaqala as a verb only as 'make reasonable' / 'be reasonable; be sensible'. In the Quran it means to understand or use one's reason (2:75 مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا عَقَلُوهُ, the refrain أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ 2:44). Added 2026-11-03.

ح.#.#.why: The lexicon reads the Form IV past أَحْيَا only as the first-person 'I live; experience' (أَحْيَا of Form I); it glosses other forms of the verb as 'enliven', so the causative sense is attested for this root. Quranic use: 2:28, 53:44 (أَمَاتَ وَأَحْيَا). Added 2026-11-03. CAMeL writes this root (ح.ي.ي) as ح.#.#.

ح.س.ب.why: The lexicon glosses ḥasiba only as 'compute; charge' / 'regard; consider', and reads the past حَسِبَ only as the preposition 'according to'. In the Quran it means to think or suppose (23:115 أَفَحَسِبْتُمْ, 104:3 يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ). Added 2026-11-03.

ر.#.#.why: The lexicon has no Form IV arā 'to show': it reads أَرَى, يُرِي and أُرِي only as Form I 'see; think' or 'kindle'. In the Quran the causative sense is frequent (20:56 أَرَيْنَاهُ آيَاتِنَا, 20:23 لِنُرِيَكَ). Added 2026-11-03. CAMeL writes this root (ر.أ.ي) as ر.#.#.

ب.ش.ر.why: The lexicon glosses bashshara only as 'rejoice; augur; evangelize' (and 'peel'). In the Quran it means to give good news, to announce glad tidings, e.g. 15:53, 37:101, 84:24. Added 2026-11-03. بَشَر: the lexicon glosses the noun only as 'joy' or 'mankind'. In the Quran it is human beings, a human (بَشَرٌ مِثْلُنَا 36:15). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 3).

ح.ش.ر.why: The lexicon reads the verb حَشَرَ only as the noun 'congregation; assemblage'; it has no verbal gloss. In the Quran ḥashara means to gather, to assemble, e.g. 19:85, 37:22. Added 2026-11-03.

ص.د.د.why: The lexicon glosses ṣadda only as 'repel; deter; resist'. In the Quran صَدَّ عَنْ is intransitive 'turn away' (4:61) and transitive 'hinder (others)' (47:1). Added 2026-11-03.

س.#.#.why: The lexicon glosses istawā only as 'be equivalent; be ripe'. In the Quran and in MSA it also means to rise, to settle (on), to be level, e.g. 11:44, 48:29, 53:6. Added 2026-11-03. CAMeL writes this root (س.و.ي) with its weak radicals as س.#.#. Also: سُوء: the lexicon glosses it 'offense; bad; ill'. The noun is evil or harm (2:49, 7:165). CAMeL writes this root (س.و.ء) with its weak radicals as #. Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 2).

ن.س.#.why: The lexicon reads the past نَسِيَ only as the noun nasy ('forgetfulness; oblivion'), although it glosses the other forms of this verb as 'forget' (نَسُوا, نَسِيتُ). Quranic use: 20:88, 20:115. Added 2026-11-03. CAMeL writes this root (ن.س.ي) as ن.س.#.

ب.غ.#.why: The lexicon glosses ibtaghā only as 'desire; want'. Its Quranic and standard sense is to seek, e.g. 17:57, 23:7. Added 2026-11-03. CAMeL writes this root (ب.غ.ي) as ب.غ.#.

ق.#.م.why: The lexicon glosses qāma only as 'undertake; carry out' and 'straighten'; it lacks the core sense to stand (up), to rise, e.g. 72:19, 73:2. Added 2026-11-03. CAMeL writes this root (ق.و.م) as ق.#.م.

ع.ر.ض.why: The lexicon glosses Form IV aʿraḍa only as 'avoid; expose; exhibit'. In the Quran أَعْرَضَ عَنْ means to turn away (from), e.g. 32:30, 41:4. Added 2026-11-03.

ع.س.#.why: The analyzer reads عَسَى only as nouns ('night patrol', 'capable'); it has no reading of the inflexible verb, whose meaning is 'perhaps, it may be that', e.g. 2:216, 27:72. Added 2026-11-03. CAMeL writes this root (ع.س.ي) as ع.س.#.

ج.ه.د.why: The CAMeL lexicon glosses the verb jāhada only as 'wage war or Jihad (against)'; its own noun gloss for the root is 'striving; endeavoring'. In the Quran the verb is to strive and exert oneself (29:6, 29:69), which is the sense the practice sentences teach. Added 2026-11-04.

ع.ص.#.why: The lexicon glosses ʿaṣā only as 'resist; refuse'. In the Quran it means to disobey (20:93, 20:121, 18:69). Added 2026-11-04.

#.ذ.ن.why: The lexicon glosses adhina as 'authorize; listen' and 'announce'; its noun gloss for the root is 'permission; authorization'. In the Quran adhina li means to permit (9:43, 22:39). Added 2026-11-04.

ج.#.ب.why: The lexicon glosses istajāba only as 'comply; reply', while it glosses ajāba of the same root as 'answer'. In the Quran istajāba is to answer or respond (2:186, 8:24). Added 2026-11-04.

ف.ت.ن.why: The lexicon glosses fatana only as 'entice; torment' and 'be infatuated', yet glosses maftūn 'fascinated; charmed' and fātin 'tempting; charming' of the same root. The practice sentences use the everyday MSA sense 'to charm, captivate'. Added 2026-11-04.

غ.ن.#.why: The lexicon glosses aghnā as 'enrich; satisfy', but reads its imperative أَغْنِ only as other words (buzz, melodious, become rich). 'Enrich' is the root's own attested verb gloss. Added 2026-11-04.

spelling:تُبْ.why: CAMeL reads the hollow imperative تُبْ (repent!, root ت.و.ب, cf. توبوا 66:8) only as تَبَّ 'perish' (root ت.ب.ب). A root exception would have to be filed under ت.ب.ب, so it is excepted by this spelling alone. Added 2026-11-04.

spelling:ذَرِ.why: CAMeL reads the imperative ذَرْ / ذَرِ (leave! let!, root و.ذ.ر, cf. ذَرْهُمْ 15:3) only as a noun of ذ.ر.ر 'strewing'; it has no analysis under و.ذ.ر, so it is excepted by this spelling alone. Added 2026-11-04.

س.ل.م.why: The CAMeL MSA lexicon glosses أَسْلَمَ only as 'hand over; surrender'. Its everyday sense — and the one learners meet first — is to become Muslim, to embrace Islam (cf. أَسْلَمَ in 3:20, 49:17). Added 2026-11-04.

spelling:ارْجُوا.why: CAMeL reads the imperative ارْجُوا (hope!, root ر.ج.و, cf. وَارْجُوا 29:36) only as a form of أَرِجَ 'be aromatic' (root أ.ر.ج); it has no analysis under ر.ج.و, so it is excepted by this spelling alone. Added 2026-11-04.

spelling:هَبْ.why: CAMeL reads the imperative هَبْ (grant!, root و.ه.ب, cf. هَبْ لِي 3:38) only as هَبَّ 'blow, get up' (root ه.ب.ب); it has no analysis under و.ه.ب, so it is excepted by this spelling alone. Added 2026-11-04.

ح.ق.ق.why: The CAMeL MSA lexicon glosses the verb حَقَّ only as 'be correct; be right'. Its other core sense — to become due, binding or incumbent (حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ, cf. فَحَقَّ عَلَيْنَا قَوْلُ رَبِّنَا 37:31, حَقَّتْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ 10:33) — is missing. Added 2026-11-04.

ف.ص.ل.why: The lexicon glosses Form II فَصَّلَ only as separate, detach, classify. Its standard and Quranic sense is to set out in detail, to explain in detail (فَصَّلْنَا الْآيَاتِ 6:126, نُفَصِّلُ 7:174). Added 2026-11-04. Form I فَصَلَ فِي / بَيْنَ 'to decide, to judge between' (32:25 يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمْ) is missing too. Extended 2026-11-04 (ranks 475–499).

س.ر.ر.why: The lexicon glosses Form IV أَسَرَّ only as confide (and reads أَسَرَّ as nouns). Its Quranic sense is to keep secret, to conceal (أَسَرُّوا النَّجْوَى 20:62, مَا تُسِرُّونَ 16:19, وَأَسِرُّوا قَوْلَكُمْ 67:13). Added 2026-11-04.

ب.#.ن.why: The lexicon glosses Form V تَبَيَّنَ as become clear, appear, explain. With an object it also means to verify, to ascertain (فَتَبَيَّنُوا 49:6, 4:94). Added 2026-11-04. CAMeL writes this root as ب.#.ن.

spelling:أَعِدْ.why: CAMeL reads the hollow Form IV imperative أَعِدْ (give back!, repeat!, of أَعَادَ, root ع.#.د; cf. يُعِيدُ 85:13) only under ع.د.د (prepare) and و.ع.د (promise), so it is excepted by this spelling alone. Added 2026-11-04.

ظ.ه.ر.why: The lexicon reads ظُهُور only as the verbal noun 'appearance, emergence'; it is also the plural of ظَهْر 'back' (عَلَى ظُهُورِهِمْ, cf. 6:31, 3:187). Added 2026-11-04.

س.#.ر.why: CAMeL reads the imperative سِيرُوا (travel!, 27:69) only as Form II سَيَّرَ 'set in motion; dispatch'. Walking and travelling are the plain senses of سَارَ يَسِيرُ (cf. 30:9 أَوَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ). Added 2026-11-04.

spelling:مَنَّ.why: CAMeL has no verb مَنَّ يَمُنُّ (to bestow a favour, 20:37 مَنَنَّا; to remind of a favour, 74:6); it reads مَنَّ only as the particles مِنْ / مَنْ, so it is excepted by this spelling alone. Added 2026-11-04.

spelling:يَمُنُّ.why: CAMeL has no verb مَنَّ يَمُنُّ (to bestow a favour; to remind someone of a favour done, cf. 49:17 يَمُنُّونَ عَلَيْكَ); it reads يَمُنُّ only under #.م.ن (Yemen, be lucky) and م.ن.# (afflict), so it is excepted by this spelling alone. Added 2026-11-04.

spelling:يَمُنُّونَ.why: As يَمُنُّ: CAMeL reads يَمُنُّونَ (49:17) only under م.ن.# (afflict; raise hopes), not as مَنَّ 'to remind of a favour', so it is excepted by this spelling alone. Added 2026-11-04.

ن.ه.#.why: CAMeL glosses Form VIII اِنْتَهَى only as 'be concluded; be completed'. Its Quranic sense is 'desist, stop' (فَإِنِ انْتَهَوْا 2:192; لَئِن لَّمْ يَنتَهِ 96:15), and with مِنْ it is the everyday 'finish'. Added 2026-11-04.

#.خ.ر.why: CAMeL has no Form II أَخَّرَ 'delay, postpone' (82:5 وَأَخَّرَتْ, 11:104 نُؤَخِّرُهُ); it reads أَخَّرَ / أَخَّرْنَا only as آخَر / آخِر 'other; last'. Added 2026-11-04.

spelling:أَخَّرَتْ.why: CAMeL reads أَخَّرَتْ (she delayed, 82:5) only under خ.ر.ت (perforate), not as Form II أَخَّرَ of #.خ.ر, so it is excepted by this spelling alone. Added 2026-11-04.

#.ذ.#.why: CAMeL glosses آذَى يُؤْذِي only as 'injure; prejudice'; its plain sense is 'harm, hurt, bother' (33:58 يُؤْذُونَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ). Added 2026-11-04.

spelling:أَبْدِ.why: CAMeL does not read أَبْدِ as the Form IV imperative of أَبْدَى 'show, express' (glossed 'express; demonstrate; show' for أَبْدَى itself); it reads it only as أَبَد 'eternity' and other roots, so it is excepted by this spelling alone. Added 2026-11-04.

س.ك.ن.why: CAMeL glosses سَكَنَ only 'be calm; calm' and Form IV 'give lodging'. سَكَنَ فِي 'live in, dwell' is its common sense in the Quran and MSA (14:45 وَسَكَنتُمْ فِي مَسَاكِنِ; 7:161 اسْكُنُوا). Added 2026-11-04.

ص.ن.ع.why: CAMeL glosses صَنَعَ as 'manufacture; fabricate; design; build' but not plain 'make', its basic sense (11:37 وَاصْنَعِ الْفُلْكَ; 20:69 مَا صَنَعُوا). Added 2026-11-04.

ص.ر.ف.why: CAMeL glosses صَرَفَ only as 'divert; spend' and 'exchange'. Its basic sense, and the one the Quran uses, is to turn (something) away or avert it (12:34 فَصَرَفَ عَنْهُ كَيْدَهُنَّ, 25:65 ٱصْرِفْ عَنَّا), still current in صَرَفَ نَظَرَهُ 'he turned his gaze away'. Form II صَرَّفَ adds to vary, set forth in various ways (6:105 نُصَرِّفُ ٱلْءَايَٰتِ) and its everyday grammar sense to conjugate (صَرَّفَ الْفِعْلَ, whence تَصْرِيف), neither of which CAMeL glosses. Added 2026-11-04.

ر.ب.ص.why: CAMeL glosses تَرَبَّصَ only as 'lay an ambush'. Its Quranic and classical sense is to wait, to await (2:228 يَتَرَبَّصْنَ بِأَنفُسِهِنَّ, 52:31 تَرَبَّصُوا۟ 'wait!'), which is the sense the card teaches. Added 2026-11-04.

spelling:اُحْلُلْ.why: CAMeL glosses the Form I present يَحُلُّ as 'dissolve; untie' but reads the unassimilated imperative اُحْلُلْ (20:27 وَٱحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً) only as 'analyze; dissolve; legalize'. 'untie' is the sense of this imperative. Added 2026-11-04.

ط.غ.#.why: The lexicon glosses ṭaghā only figuratively ('overstep; be excessive; be tyrannical'); its literal sense, water or a river rising over its banks (طَغَى النَّهْرُ, cf. 69:11), is the root's basic meaning in the dictionaries. طَغَى بِـ is also to grow insolent, arrogant through something (wealth, power) — the lexicon's 'be tyrannical' is the outward side of it. Added 2026-11-04.

ز.ك.#.why: CAMeL reads the Form II present يُزَكِّي / يُزَكُّونَ only as nouns of #.ز.ك (guards) and has no verb gloss for zakkā 'to purify; to pay the zakat on (one's wealth)', cf. 91:9 قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن زَكَّاهَا. Added 2026-11-04.

س.ق.#.why: The lexicon glosses saqā as 'give to drink; irrigate'; 'water' (plants, a garden) is the everyday English for the same sense. Added 2026-11-04.

spelling:صِفْ.why: CAMeL reads the imperative صِفْ (describe!, root و.ص.ف) only as the noun صَفّ 'line, row' (root ص.ف.ف); it has no analysis under و.ص.ف, so it is excepted by this spelling alone. Added 2026-11-04.

spelling:أَقْطَعُ.why: CAMeL reads أَقْطَعُ only as the Form IV past أَقْطَعَ or the adjective 'amputee'; it has no first-person present of qaṭaʿa 'I cut', so it is excepted by this spelling alone. Added 2026-11-04.

#.ر.ث.why: The lexicon glosses Form IV awratha only as 'bequeath'; its common figurative sense is to cause, to result in (الْكَسَلُ يُورِثُ النَّدَمَ 'laziness causes regret'). Added 2026-11-04.

ع.ه.د.why: CAMeL glosses Form III عَاهَدَ only as 'contract with; conclude an alliance with'. Its everyday sense is to pledge, to promise solemnly (عَاهَدَ نَفْسَهُ عَلَى الصَّبْرِ 'he pledged himself to patience'; cf. 33:23 صَدَقُوا۟ مَا عَٰهَدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ عَلَيْهِ). Added 2026-11-04.

ث.ب.ت.why: CAMeL glosses Form II ثَبَّتَ as 'confirm; reinforce' and reads its imperatives as 'be firm'. Its basic sense, the Quran's (47:7 وَيُثَبِّتْ أَقْدَامَكُمْ) and the everyday one, is to make firm, fasten, fix in place (ثَبَّتَ الرَّفَّ 'he fixed the shelf'). Added 2026-11-04.

spelling:أُوقِنُ.why: CAMeL reads أُوقِنُ only as أَوْقَ 'burden' (root #.#.ق); it has no first-person present of Form IV أَيْقَنَ 'I am certain' (root #.ق.ن, cf. يُوقِنُونَ 45:20), so it is excepted by this spelling alone. Added 2026-11-04.

spelling:اِبْنُوا.why: CAMeL reads the imperative اِبْنُوا (build!, root ب.ن.ي, cf. 37:97 ٱبْنُوا۟) only as أَبَّنَ 'eulogize' (root #.ب.ن); its analysis under ب.ن.# is missing, so it is excepted by this spelling alone. Added 2026-11-04.

spelling:قِ.why: The doubly weak imperative قِ (protect!, root و.ق.ي, cf. قُوا 66:6) is a single letter, which CAMeL reads only as the letter name Q; the lexicon glosses the verb يَقِي 'preserve; safeguard' elsewhere, so it is excepted by this spelling alone. Added 2026-11-04.

spelling:أَمْدِدْ.why: CAMeL reads the Form IV imperative أَمْدِدْ (provide!, cf. أَمَدَّكُم 26:133) only as the Form I jussive 'I extend'; it glosses the Form IV verb أَمَدَّ 'provide; furnish' elsewhere, so it is excepted by this spelling alone. Added 2026-11-04.

spelling:اِرْكَبُوا.why: CAMeL reads the imperative اِرْكَبُوا (ride! / get in!, cf. ٱرْكَبُوا۟ فِيهَا 11:41) only as the Form IV past أَرْكَبُوا 'make ride', so it is excepted by this spelling alone. Added 2026-11-04.

ن.ب.ذ.why: CAMeL glosses the past نَبَذَ only as the noun نَبْذ 'discarding; rejection' and has no verb analysis of it, though it glosses the same root's verb as 'discard; reject' (اِنْبِذْ). Quranic use: 2:101, 3:187. Added 2026-11-04.

ر.د.د.why: The lexicon glosses Form VIII irtadda only as 'revert; forsake; refrain' (the apostasy sense). Its literal sense, to go or come back, is the Quran's in 12:96 (فَارْتَدَّ بَصِيرًا), 18:64 (فَارْتَدَّا عَلَى آثَارِهِمَا) and 14:43 (لَا يَرْتَدُّ إِلَيْهِمْ طَرْفُهُمْ), and everyday MSA (اِرْتَدَّ الصَّوْتُ, the sound bounced back). Added 2026-11-04.

ر.#.د.why: The lexicon glosses rāwada only as 'entice; seduce' (its sense in 12:23, 54:37). In everyday MSA a thought, a hope or a dream is its subject (رَاوَدَنِي أَمَلٌ, a hope came over me; يُرَاوِدُنِي حُلُمٌ, a dream keeps coming back to me); practice sentences use only that sense, never the seduction one. CAMeL writes this root with its weak radical as ر.#.د. Added 2026-11-04.

spelling:سَمِّ.why: CAMeL reads the imperative سَمِّ (name!, of سَمَّى يُسَمِّي) only as سَمّ 'poison' under س.م.م, so it is excepted by this spelling alone. Added 2026-11-04.

spelling:اِهْبِطُوا.why: CAMeL glosses the imperative اِهْبِطُوا (go down!, cf. ٱهْبِطُوا۟ 7:24) only as the Form IV past أَهْبَطُوا 'lower, reduce', so it is excepted by this spelling alone. Added 2026-11-04.

ع.ل.#.why: The lexicon glosses tafāʿala تَعَالَى only as 'be raised; be exalted'. In ordinary Arabic it also means to rise (تَعَالَى الضَّجِيجُ, تَعَالَتِ الأَصْوَاتُ), to rise above (تَعَالَى عَلَى خِلَافَاتِهِ) and, with عَلَى a person, to act superior; its imperative is 'come!' (تَعَالَوْا 3:64, which the lexicon itself glosses 'come!'). Added 2026-11-04. CAMeL writes this root (ع.ل.و) with its weak radical as ع.ل.#.

spelling:تَعَالَ.why: CAMeL reads the masculine singular imperative تَعَالَ (come!, cf. تَعَالَوْا 3:61, تَعَالَيْنَ 33:28) only under ع.#.ل 'be supported', though it glosses the feminine and plural imperatives of ع.ل.و as 'come!', so it is excepted by this spelling alone. Added 2026-11-04.

ض.ع.ف.why: The lexicon glosses the Form X اِسْتَضْعَفَ only as 'despise; oppress'. Its core sense is to deem someone weak (and so take advantage of them), cf. ٱسْتُضْعِفُوا۟ 'those deemed weak' 4:75, 28:5; 'despise' is a different verb (اِحْتَقَرَ). Added 2026-11-04.

ع.ز.ل.why: The lexicon glosses ifta'ala اِعْتَزَلَ only as 'be separate; be dissociated'. In ordinary Arabic it means to withdraw from or keep away from something or someone (اِعْتَزَلَ النَّاسَ, cf. 44:21 فَٱعْتَزِلُونِ 'keep away from me') and, of a player or official, to retire. Added 2026-11-04.

ف.#.ض.why: The lexicon glosses af'ala أَفَاضَ only as 'spill; overfill'. With فِي it is to elaborate, to speak at length (أَفَاضَ فِي الشَّرْحِ); of a crowd it is to pour out, to depart in a throng (2:199 ثُمَّ أَفِيضُوا۟ مِنْ حَيْثُ أَفَاضَ ٱلنَّاسُ). Added 2026-11-04. CAMeL writes this root (ف.ي.ض) with its weak radical as ف.#.ض.

ن.ص.ر.why: The lexicon glosses ifta'ala اِنْتَصَرَ only as 'be victorious'. Its everyday sense is to win (اِنْتَصَرَ الْفَرِيقُ 'the team won') and, with عَلَى, to triumph over, to overcome. Added 2026-11-04. أَنْصَار, plural of نَصِير: the lexicon reads it only as the proper name Ansar. It means supporters, helpers (مَنْ أَنصَارِىٓ 3:52). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 3).

ن.ز.ل.why: The lexicon glosses tafa''ala تَنَزَّلَ only as 'condescend'. Its basic sense is to come down, to descend (gradually) — the Quran's own use (26:222 تَنَزَّلُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ أَفَّاكٍ, 97:4 تَنَزَّلُ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ). Added 2026-11-04.

spelling:شَاقُّوا.why: CAMeL reads شَاقُّوا only as شَاقَ يَشُوقُ 'please, delight' (root ش.و.ق), but it is the Form III past of ش.ق.ق, شَاقَّ 'to oppose, to defy' (59:4 شَآقُّوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ), so it is excepted by this spelling. Added 2026-11-04.

spelling:أَشْهِدُوا.why: CAMeL reads the Form IV imperative أَشْهِدُوا (cf. 2:282 وَأَشْهِدُوٓا۟) only as 'quote', but أَشْهَدَ is 'to call to witness, to take as witness', as it glosses the present يُشْهِدُ. Added 2026-11-04.

spelling:اِحْفَظُوا.why: CAMeL reads اِحْفَظُوا only as the Form IV past أَحْفَظُوا 'they annoyed', missing the hamzat-wasl imperative of حَفِظَ يَحْفَظُ 'protect, preserve, keep' (cf. 5:89 وَٱحْفَظُوٓا۟ أَيْمَٰنَكُمْ), which it glosses so in the past and present, so it is excepted by this spelling. Added 2026-11-04.

ح.ف.ظ.why: The CAMeL MSA lexicon glosses ḥafiẓa only as 'preserve; protect; maintain'. Its everyday sense is also to memorize, to learn by heart (حَفِظَ الْقُرْآنَ, حَافِظ 'one who knows the Quran by heart'), standard in every Arabic dictionary. Owner-approved; added 2026-11-04.

#.ز.ر.why: The lexicon glosses wazara only as 'commit a sin' (and وَزَرَ as other roots' 'button up', 'rebuke'). Its Quranic sense is to bear, to carry a burden or a sin (6:164, 17:15, 35:18, 53:38 أَلَّا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَى; وِزْر 'burden'). Added 2026-11-04. CAMeL writes this root (و.ز.ر) as #.ز.ر.

ث.ق.ف.why: The lexicon glosses thaqifa only in modern senses ('be skillful; be clever; instruct; educate'). In the Quran it means to come upon, find, overtake (2:191, 4:91, 8:57, 33:61, 60:2); classical dictionaries also give ثَقِفَ الشَّيْءَ 'to grasp it quickly', the root of the modern 'skillful'. Added 2026-11-04.

spelling:أَسْرِ.why: CAMeL reads the Form IV imperative أَسْرِ only as أَسَرَ 'capture' or أَسَرَّ 'confide', missing أَسْرَى 'to travel by night' (11:81, 15:65, 20:77, 26:52, 44:23 فَأَسْرِ), which it glosses so in the past, so it is excepted by this spelling. Added 2026-11-04. CAMeL writes this root (س.ر.ي) as س.ر.#.

spelling:اُدْلُلْ.why: CAMeL reads the hamzat-wasl imperative اُدْلُلْ (the unassimilated form of دُلَّ 'show the way!') only as a first-person present 'I prove; I pamper', missing the imperative of دَلَّ يَدُلُّ 'point, indicate', which it glosses so in the past (cf. 20:120 هَلْ أَدُلُّكَ). It is excepted by this spelling alone. Added 2026-11-04.

ف.ج.ر.why: The lexicon glosses Form II فَجَّرَ only as 'detonate; break ground' (and the root's Form I as 'live immorally'). Its Quranic sense is to make water gush forth, to cause springs to burst out (17:91, 18:33, 36:34, 54:12 وَفَجَّرْنَا الْأَرْضَ عُيُونًا, 76:6), and in everyday Arabic فَجَّرَ الْبَالُونَ 'burst (a balloon)'. Added 2026-11-04.

#.س.ع.why: The lexicon glosses وَسِعَ only as 'be spacious, be wide, be able'. Its transitive sense is to encompass, to have room for, to hold (2:255 وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ, 6:80, 20:98, 40:7); the dictionaries give وَسِعَهُ الْمَكَانُ 'the place held him'. Added 2026-11-04. CAMeL writes this root (و.س.ع) as #.س.ع.

#.د.#.why: The lexicon glosses أَدَّى only as 'direct, guide, lead' and 'pay blood money'. Its common sense is to perform, carry out, pay, deliver (2:178 وَأَدَاءٌ إِلَيْهِ, 2:283 فَلْيُؤَدِّ الَّذِي اؤْتُمِنَ أَمَانَتَهُ, 3:75, 4:58 أَنْ تُؤَدُّوا الْأَمَانَاتِ, 44:18 أَدُّوا إِلَيَّ); modern أَدَّى وَاجِبَهُ 'did his duty', أَدَّى دَيْنَهُ 'paid his debt'. Added 2026-11-04. CAMeL writes this root (أ.د.ي) as #.د.#.

#.ل.ف.why: The lexicon glosses the past أَلَّفَ only as 'befriend, adapt, familiarize' (and 'compose' only in the present). Its Quranic sense is to unite, to bring hearts together (3:103 فَأَلَّفَ بَيْنَ قُلُوبِكُمْ, 8:63, 24:43), and in everyday Arabic أَلَّفَ كِتَابًا 'composed, wrote a book'. Added 2026-11-04. CAMeL writes this root (أ.ل.ف) as #.ل.ف.

ب.خ.س.why: The lexicon glosses بَخَسَ only as 'depreciate, underestimate'. Its Quranic and everyday sense is to cheat someone of what is due, to diminish it (2:282 وَلَا يَبْخَسْ مِنْهُ شَيْئًا, 7:85, 11:15, 11:85, 26:183). Added 2026-11-04.

ب.ر.#.why: The lexicon glosses Form V تَبَرَّأَ only as 'be absolved, be innocent'. With مِنْ it means to disown, to dissociate oneself from (2:166–167 إِذْ تَبَرَّأَ الَّذِينَ اتُّبِعُوا, 9:114, 28:63 تَبَرَّأْنَا إِلَيْكَ, 59:16). Added 2026-11-04. CAMeL writes this root (ب.ر.أ) as ب.ر.#.

spelling:أَدِّ.why: CAMeL reads the Form II imperative أَدِّ only as أَدَّ (root أ.د.د, 'befall; burden; horrible'), missing the imperative of أَدَّى 'perform, pay, deliver' (cf. 44:18 أَدُّوا إِلَيَّ), so it is excepted by this spelling alone. Added 2026-11-04. CAMeL writes this root (أ.د.ي) as #.د.#.

ث.#.ر.why: The lexicon glosses Form IV أَثَارَ only as 'provoke, agitate' (and 'take revenge'). Its Quranic and everyday sense is to stir up, to raise dust or clouds, to plough up the earth (30:9 وَأَثَارُوا الْأَرْضَ, 30:48 فَتُثِيرُ سَحَابًا, 100:4 فَأَثَرْنَ بِهِ نَقْعًا). Added 2026-11-04. CAMeL writes this root (ث.و.ر) as ث.#.ر.

ج.ه.ل.why: The lexicon glosses جَهِلَ only as 'ignore' and 'call stupid'. Its Quranic and everyday sense is not to know, to be ignorant of (12:89 إِذْ أَنْتُمْ جَاهِلُونَ, 27:55 بَلْ أَنْتُمْ قَوْمٌ تَجْهَلُونَ, 6:111). Added 2026-11-04.

ح.م.ل.why: The lexicon glosses Form II حَمَّلَ as 'make carry, impose, charge with' but not 'load'. Loading a beast or a vehicle (making it carry a load) is its plainest everyday sense, and 'burden' its Quranic one (2:286 وَلَا تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِ, 24:54). Added 2026-11-04. حِمْل: the lexicon reads the noun as حَمْل 'urging'; in the Quran it is a load, a burden carried (12:72 حِمْلُ بَعِيرٍ). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 12).

ج.م.ر.why: The lexicon glosses جَمْرَة only as 'ember, pebble'. In the rites of Hajj الْجَمْرَة / الْجَمَرَات is the name of the three stone pillars at Mina that pilgrims pelt (جَمْرَةُ الْعَقَبَةِ), and 'pillar' is how it is translated. Added 2026-11-04.

ع.ق.ر.why: The lexicon glosses the root only as 'barren, sterile' (عَاقِر, عُقْم) and the noun عُقْر 'within'. The verb عَقَرَ يَعْقِرُ 'to hamstring, to wound' (فَعَقَرُوهَا 26:157; كَلْبٌ عَقُور 'a biting dog') is missing. Added 2026-11-04.

غ.ل.ل.why: The lexicon has غَلَّ only as 'shackle' and the noun غِلّ 'rancor'. The Quran's غَلَّ يَغُلُّ 'to embezzle, to take by fraud' (3:161 وَمَا كَانَ لِنَبِيٍّ أَنْ يَغُلَّ; غُلُول) is missing. Added 2026-11-04.

ق.ر.ر.why: The lexicon has قَرَّ only as 'settle down, remain'. The idiom قَرَّ عَيْنًا / قَرَّتْ عَيْنُهُ 'to be delighted, comforted' (lit. 'his eye was cooled'; 20:40 كَيْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا, 19:26 وَقَرِّي عَيْنًا), the sense this verb teaches, is missing. Added 2026-11-04.

spelling:أَفْتِ.why: CAMeL reads the defective Form IV imperative أَفْتِ (give a legal opinion!, cf. أَفْتُونِي 27:32) only as Form I 'be youthful' (root ف.ت.#) or ف.ت.ت 'weaken'. A root exception under ف.ت.# would admit 'fatwa' for every spelling of that root, so it is excepted by this spelling alone. Added 2026-11-04.

غ.ل.ق.why: The CAMeL lexicon glosses أَغْلَقَ only as 'lock or bolt shut'; in MSA it is the ordinary verb 'to close' (a door, a shop); 'lock' is أَقْفَلَ. Added 2026-11-05 for the noun pilot (blind reviewer refused 'locked').

ع.ذ.ب.why: عَذْب of water is 'fresh' (sweet, drinkable: مَاءٌ عَذْبٌ); the lexicon has only 'sweet;pleasant', which misleads in English. Added 2026-11-05 for the noun pilot.

م.ل.ك.why: مَلَك: the lexicon reads the singular only as مُلْك/مَلِك (dominion, king, property) though it glosses the plural مَلَائِكَة 'angels'. The Quran's مَلَك is an angel (ٱلْمَلَكُ 69:17, 6:8). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 2). مَالِك: the lexicon glosses it as 'proprietor; holder'; 'owner' is the plain English word (36:71 فَهُمْ لَهَا مَالِكُونَ). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 11).

ف.ض.ل.why: فَضْل: the lexicon glosses it only as 'distinction; quality; superiority'. In the Quran it is favor or bounty (2:64, 62:4), and in MSA أَهْلُ الْفَضْلِ are people of virtue. Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 2).

ص.ل.ح.why: صَالِح/صَالِحَة: the lexicon has 'pious; upright' and 'advantage'. The Quranic noun is the righteous (ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ 2:130), the standard English rendering. Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 2).

ن.ذ.ر.why: نَذِير: the lexicon glosses it only as the thing, 'warning; alarm'. In the Quran it is mostly the person, a warner (إِنْ أَنتَ إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ 35:23). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 2).

ش.ه.د.why: شَهِيد: the lexicon glosses it only as 'martyr'. In the Quran it is mostly a witness (وَٱسْتَشْهِدُوا۟ شَهِيدَيْنِ 2:282). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 2).

ع.ر.ف.why: مَعْرُوف: the lexicon glosses it only as the adjective 'known'. In the Quran it is mostly a noun, what is right and kind (بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ 2:178, قَوْلٌ مَعْرُوفٌ 2:263). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 3).

ح.س.ن.why: مُحْسِن: the lexicon glosses it only as 'embellisher'. In the Quran it is one who does good (إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ 2:195). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 3).

ف.س.ق.why: فَاسِق: the lexicon glosses it only as 'adulterer'. In the Quran it is one who defiantly disobeys, a transgressor (وَأَكْثَرُهُمُ ٱلْفَٰسِقُونَ 3:110). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 3).

ر.س.ل.why: مُرْسَل: the lexicon glosses it only as the participle 'sent'. As a noun it is one sent, an envoy (إِنَّكَ لَمِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ 36:3). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 3).

ن.ع.م.why: نَعَم: the lexicon reads نعم only as 'yes' or a verb. The Quran's ٱلنَّعَمِ (5:95) and ٱلْأَنْعَٰم are livestock. Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 3).

م.ل.#.why: مَلَأ: the lexicon reads it only as the verb 'be bored'. In the Quran ٱلْمَلَأُ is the chiefs, the council of a people (7:60). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 3).

س.ل.ط.ن.why: سُلْطَان: the lexicon glosses it only as the title 'Sultan'. In the Quran it is authority or a proof (بِسُلْطَٰنٍ مُبِينٍ 11:96). CAMeL keys سُلْطَان under the four-letter root س.ل.ط.ن. Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 3).

ح.د.ث.why: حَدِيث: the lexicon glosses the noun only as 'Hadith (Islamic tradition)'. In the Quran it is a story or talk (هَلْ أَتَاكَ حَدِيثُ مُوسَى 20:9; فَبِأَيِّ حَدِيثٍ 77:50). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 4).

ب.ط.ل.why: بَاطِل: the lexicon glosses it only as the adjective 'void; false'. As a noun in the Quran it is falsehood (وَلَا تَلْبِسُوا الْحَقَّ بِالْبَاطِلِ 2:42). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 4).

ك.#.د.why: كَيْد: the lexicon glosses it 'stratagem; ruse'. In the Quran it is a plot or scheme (إِنَّهُ مِنْ كَيْدِكُنَّ 12:28). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 4).

ب.#.س.why: بَأْس: the lexicon glosses it only from the idiom لَا بَأْسَ ('bad; objection'). In the Quran it is might in battle and harm (أُولِي بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ 17:5; فَمَنْ يَنْصُرُنَا مِنْ بَأْسِ اللَّهِ 40:29). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 4).

ط.#.ف.why: طَائِفَة: the lexicon glosses it 'sect; party; faction'. In the Quran it is a group of people (طَائِفَةٌ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ 24:2). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 4).

ذ.ك.ر.why: ذِكْرَى: the lexicon glosses it 'commemoration; remembrance'; in everyday Arabic ذِكْرَى is a memory (ذِكْرَى جَمِيلَةٌ), the sense the practice sentences use. Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 4).

ف.ل.ك.why: فُلْك: the lexicon knows only فَلَك 'celestial body; orbit'. In the Quran الْفُلْك is a ship or ships (فِي الْفُلْكِ الْمَشْحُونِ 36:41). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 4).

ف.س.د.why: مُفْسِد: the lexicon glosses it only as the adjective 'corrupt; corrupting'. As a noun in the Quran it is one who spreads corruption (إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُفْسِدِينَ 28:77). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 4).

ض.ر.ر.why: ضُرّ: the lexicon glosses it only as 'polygamy' (ضَرَّة, a co-wife). In the Quran it is harm, affliction (وَإِذَا مَسَّ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ ٱلضُّرُّ 10:12). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 5).

م.ك.ر.why: مَكْر: the lexicon glosses it 'deception; double-dealing'. In the Quran it is scheming, plotting (وَمَكَرُوا۟ وَمَكَرَ ٱللَّهُ 3:54). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 5).

ظ.ل.ل.why: ظِلّ: the lexicon glosses it only figuratively, 'patronage; shelter'. Its first sense, in the Quran too, is shade (وَظِلٍّ مَّمْدُودٍ 56:30). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 5). ظُلَّة: the lexicon glosses it 'veranda', and 'shelter' only with a possessive suffix; in the Quran it is a shelter or canopy overhead (7:171, 26:189). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 9).

ف.ح.ش.why: فَاحِشَة: the lexicon glosses it only as an adjective ('monstrous; obscene') or a person. As a noun it is an indecency, a shameful deed (وَلَا تَقْرَبُوا۟ ٱلْفَوَٰحِشَ 6:151). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 5).

س.ر.ف.why: مُسْرِف: the lexicon glosses it only as the adjective 'excessive'. As a noun it is one who goes to excess, a spendthrift (وَلَا تُسْرِفُوٓا۟ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ 7:31). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 5).

ن.ك.ر.why: مُنكَر: the lexicon glosses it as an adjective ('denied; reprehensible') or a denier. As a noun it is wrongdoing, what is recognised as wrong (وَيَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ ٱلْمُنكَرِ 3:104). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 5).

س.ن.ن.why: سُنَّة: the lexicon glosses it 'customary procedure; enactment; tooth'. In the Quran it is a way, a custom (سُنَّةَ مَن قَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا 17:77); 'customary' alone does not match 'custom' in base form. Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 5).

ب.ل.غ.why: بَلَاغ: the lexicon glosses it 'communique; report; notice'. In the Quran it is the message conveyed (هَٰذَا بَلَٰغٌ لِّلنَّاسِ 14:52). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 5).

ز.#.ن.why: زِينَة: the lexicon glosses it 'embellishment; decoration'. The standard rendering of the Quranic sense is adornment (ٱلْمَالُ وَٱلْبَنُونَ زِينَةُ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا 18:46). CAMeL writes this root (ز.ي.ن) as ز.#.ن. Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 5).

ت.ر.ب.why: تُرَاب: the lexicon glosses it 'dirt; soil'. In the Quran, and in its standard rendering, it is dust (خَلَقَهُۥ مِن تُرَابٍ 3:59). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 5).

ز.ر.ع.why: The CAMeL MSA lexicon glosses زَرْع only as 'planting'. In the Quran it is the crops in the field (زُرُوعٍ وَمَقَامٍ كَرِيمٍ 44:26, وَزَرْعٍ وَنَخِيلٍ 26:148). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 6).

ع.ش.#.why: The lexicon glosses عَشِيّ only as nest/night-blindness. In the Quran it is the evening (بِٱلْعَشِيِّ وَٱلْإِبْكَٰرِ 3:41). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 6).

ح.ر.ث.why: The CAMeL MSA lexicon glosses حَرْث only as 'plowing; cultivation'. In the Quran it is the tilled land and its crops (وَيُهْلِكَ ٱلْحَرْثَ وَٱلنَّسْلَ 2:205, حَرْثَ ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ 42:20). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 6).

ع.ج.ل.why: The CAMeL MSA lexicon glosses عِجْل only as 'beef' (and the verb's hurry). In the Quran it is a calf (بِعِجْلٍ حَنِيذٍ 11:69, عِجْلًا جَسَدًا 7:148). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 6).

خ.ط.#.why: The CAMeL MSA lexicon glosses خَطِيئَة only as 'mistake; error; fault'. In the Quran it is a sin (وَأَحَٰطَتْ بِهِۦ خَطِيٓـَٔتُهُۥ 2:81, نَّغْفِرْ لَكُمْ خَطَٰيَٰكُمْ 2:58). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 6).

ر.ح.م.why: The CAMeL MSA lexicon glosses أَرْحَام only as 'kinships; wombs'. In the Quran and in MSA ذَوُو ٱلْأَرْحَامِ / صِلَةُ ٱلْأَرْحَامِ are one's relatives (وَأُو۟لُوا۟ ٱلْأَرْحَامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلَىٰ بِبَعْضٍ 8:75). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 6).

ف.#.#.why: فِئَة: the lexicon glosses it only as 'faction; party'. In the Quran it is a group, a band (كَمْ مِنْ فِئَةٍ قَلِيلَةٍ 2:249), as in MSA. CAMeL writes this root (ف.ي.ء) as ف.#.#. Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 7).

ج.ل.د.why: جُلُود: the lexicon reads the plural only as 'patient'. It is the plural of جِلْد 'skin' (كُلَّمَا نَضِجَتْ جُلُودُهُمْ 4:56). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 7).

خ.ل.ف.why: خَلِيفَة: the lexicon glosses it only as 'deputy; caliph'. In the Quran it is a successor, one who succeeds others on the earth (2:30, 38:26; خَلَائِفَ 6:165), as in MSA خَلِيفَةُ الْمُدِيرِ. Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 7).

ع.#.ج.why: عِوَج: the lexicon glosses it 'curvature; bending'. The Quranic sense is crookedness (لَمْ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ عِوَجًا 18:1, لَا تَرَى فِيهَا عِوَجًا 20:107). CAMeL writes this root (ع.و.ج) as ع.#.ج. Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 7).

ل.غ.#.why: لَغْو: the lexicon glosses it 'nonsense; null'. In the Quran it is idle talk (لَا يَسْمَعُونَ فِيهَا لَغْوًا 19:62, عَنِ اللَّغْوِ مُعْرِضُونَ 23:3). CAMeL writes this root (ل.غ.و) as ل.غ.#. Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 7).

#.ع.ظ.why: مَوْعِظَة: the lexicon glosses it 'exhortation; lecture'. The standard rendering is admonition, good counsel (وَالْمَوْعِظَةِ الْحَسَنَةِ 16:125). CAMeL writes this root (و.ع.ظ) as #.ع.ظ. Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 7).

ب.ر.ر.why: بِرّ: the lexicon glosses it 'charity; piety'. In the Quran it is righteousness, goodness toward others (لَيْسَ الْبِرَّ 2:177, تَعَاوَنُوا عَلَى الْبِرِّ 5:2). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 7).

خ.ز.ن.why: خَزَائِن: the lexicon glosses it only as 'vaults; lockers; coffers'. In the Quran it is storehouses, treasuries (خَزَائِنِ الْأَرْضِ 12:55). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 7).

ص.ع.ق.why: صَاعِقَة: the lexicon glosses it 'lightning; stunning'. In the Quran it is a thunderbolt, a deafening blast (الصَّوَاعِقَ 13:13, 2:19). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 7).

ع.ق.ب.why: عَقِب: the lexicon glosses it only as 'consequence'. In the Quran it is the heel (انْقَلَبَ عَلَى عَقِبَيْهِ 22:11, عَلَى أَعْقَابِكُمْ 3:144). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 7).

ق.ر.ن.why: قَرِين: the lexicon glosses it 'associate; comrade; spouse'. In the Quran it is a constant companion (فَهُوَ لَهُ قَرِينٌ 43:36, قَالَ قَائِلٌ مِنْهُمْ إِنِّي كَانَ لِي قَرِينٌ 37:51). Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 7).

ل.ع.ب.why: لَعِب: the lexicon vowels the noun only as لَعْب 'game; sport', so the Quranic لَعِب (لَعِبٌ وَلَهْوٌ 6:32) finds no noun analysis; 'play' is its sense, and the lexicon glosses the verb لَعِبَ as 'play'. Added 2026-11-05 (noun batch 7).

#.د.د.why: مَوَدَّة: the lexicon glosses it 'friendship; love' (and, under another spelling, 'fashion'). In the Quran it is affection between people (مَوَدَّةً وَرَحْمَةً 30:21, ٱلْمَوَدَّةَ فِي ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ 42:23), as in MSA. CAMeL writes this root (و.د.د) as #.د.د. Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 7).

ج.ه.ر.why: جَهْر: the lexicon glosses the noun only as 'notoriety'. In the Quran it is saying something aloud, openly (وَإِنْ تَجْهَرْ بِالْقَوْلِ 20:7, يَعْلَمُ الْجَهْرَ 87:7). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 8).

ح.ب.ل.why: حَبْل: the lexicon glosses it 'cord; cable' and, vowelled حَبَل, 'pregnancy'. In the Quran it is a rope (حَبْلٌ مِنْ مَسَدٍ 111:5, وَاعْتَصِمُوا بِحَبْلِ اللَّهِ 3:103 figuratively; حِبَالُهُمْ 20:66). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 8).

س.#.ل.why: سَائِل: the lexicon glosses it 'questioner; petitioner'. In the Quran it is mostly one who asks for help, a beggar (وَأَمَّا السَّائِلَ فَلَا تَنْهَرْ 93:10, لِلسَّائِلِ وَالْمَحْرُومِ 51:19). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 8).

س.ف.ر.why: سَفَر: the lexicon has only سِفْر 'book' and سُفْرَة 'dining table'. In the Quran it is a journey (أَوْ عَلَى سَفَرٍ 2:184, لَقِينَا مِنْ سَفَرِنَا هَٰذَا نَصَبًا 18:62). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 8).

س.ف.ه.why: سَفِيه: the lexicon glosses it only as the adjective 'foolish'. In the Quran it is a person, a fool (فَإِنْ كَانَ الَّذِي عَلَيْهِ الْحَقُّ سَفِيهًا 2:282, وَلَا تُؤْتُوا السُّفَهَاءَ أَمْوَالَكُمُ 4:5). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 8).

خ.ر.ج.why: إِخْرَاج: the lexicon glosses it 'production; extraction; ousting'. In the Quran it is driving people out (وَإِخْرَاجُ أَهْلِهِ مِنْهُ 2:217, عَلَى إِخْرَاجِكُمْ 60:9). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 8).

spelling:الْيَمُّ.why: يَمّ: the lexicon has no analysis of the word at all, so it is excepted by its spellings. In the Quran it is the sea or great river (فَأَلْقِيهِ فِي الْيَمِّ 28:7, فَأَغْرَقْنَاهُمْ فِي الْيَمِّ 7:136). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 8).

spelling:الْيَمَّ.why: يَمّ: the lexicon has no analysis of the word at all, so it is excepted by its spellings. In the Quran it is the sea or great river (فَأَلْقِيهِ فِي الْيَمِّ 28:7, فَأَغْرَقْنَاهُمْ فِي الْيَمِّ 7:136). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 8).

spelling:الْيَمِّ.why: يَمّ: the lexicon has no analysis of the word at all, so it is excepted by its spellings. In the Quran it is the sea or great river (فَأَلْقِيهِ فِي الْيَمِّ 28:7, فَأَغْرَقْنَاهُمْ فِي الْيَمِّ 7:136). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 8).

ذ.ل.ل.why: ذِلَّة: the lexicon glosses the bare and definite noun only as 'depravity; submissiveness' ('humiliation; dishonor' only with a possessive). In the Quran it is humiliation (ضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الذِّلَّةُ 2:61, تَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ 10:27). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 8).

خ.م.ر.why: خَمْر: the lexicon glosses it only 'liquor; alcohol'. In the Quran it is wine, the intoxicant (2:219, 5:90, 47:15). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 9).

ق.ب.ر.why: قَبْر: the lexicon's first gloss is 'lark', then 'tomb; sepulcher'. The ordinary word for a grave (9:84, 82:4 الْقُبُورُ). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 9).

ك.ب.ر.why: كِبَر: the lexicon glosses it 'magnitude; grandeur'. In the Quran it is old age (2:266 وَأَصَابَهُ الْكِبَرُ, 3:40, 15:54). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 9).

ب.ل.د.why: بَلْدَة: the lexicon glosses it 'township'. In the Quran it is a town or land (25:49 بَلْدَةً مَيْتًا, 34:15 بَلْدَةٌ طَيِّبَةٌ). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 9).

#.ك.ل.why: The lexicon glosses the verbal noun أَكْل only as 'food; meal'. In the Quran it is the act of eating (وَأَكْلِهِمُ ٱلرِّبَوٰا۟ 4:161, أَكْلًا لَّمًّا 89:19). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 10).

#.م.ن.why: The lexicon glosses أَمَانَة as 'faithfulness; loyalty; secretariat; deposit'. In the Quran it is a trust, a thing entrusted (أَمَٰنَٰتِكُمْ 8:27, لِأَمَٰنَٰتِهِمْ 23:8). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 10).

ز.#.ر.why: The lexicon glosses زُور only as 'cross-eyed; force'. In the Quran it is falsehood (قَوْلَ ٱلزُّورِ 22:30, ظُلْمًا وَزُورًا 25:4), as in MSA شَهَادَةُ الزُّورِ 'false testimony'. Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 10).

س.ر.ج.why: The lexicon glosses سِرَاج only as 'saddler' and a name. In the Quran it is a lamp (سِرَاجًا وَهَّاجًا 78:13, سِرَاجًا مُّنِيرًا 33:46). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 10).

ش.ه.ب.why: The lexicon glosses شِهَاب as 'shooting star; meteorite'. 'meteor' is the same thing in one word, and in the Quran it is also a burning flame (بِشِهَابٍ قَبَسٍ 27:7). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 10).

س.ن.ب.ل.why: The lexicon glosses سُنْبُلَة as 'spike (of grain)' and 'Virgo'. In the Quran it is an ear of grain (سَبْعَ سَنَابِلَ فِي كُلِّ سُنۢبُلَةٍ 2:261). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 10).

ف.#.ج.why: The lexicon glosses فَوْج only as 'battalion; regiment'. In the Quran it is a group or crowd of people (فَوْجًا 27:83, أَفْوَاجًا 110:2), as in MSA فَوْجٌ مِنَ السُّيَّاحِ. Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 10).

ل.#.ح.why: The lexicon glosses لَوْح only as 'blackboard; slate'. In the Quran it is a tablet (the tablets of Moses, ٱلْأَلْوَاحَ 7:145) and a plank (ذَاتِ أَلْوَٰحٍ 54:13). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 10).

ح.ل.#.why: The lexicon glosses the bare and definite حِلْيَة only as 'trinket; ornament' (jewelry only with a possessive). In the Quran it is jewelry worn as adornment (حِلْيَةً تَلْبَسُونَهَا 16:14). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 10).

ع.ص.ب.why: عُصْبَة: the lexicon glosses it only as 'clan; league; federation'. In the Quran it is a group or band of people (12:8 وَنَحْنُ عُصْبَةٌ; 24:11). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 11).

ع.ق.د.why: عُقْدَة: the lexicon glosses it only as 'complex' or 'contract'. In the Quran it is a knot (20:27 وَاحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِنْ لِسَانِي; 113:4 فِي الْعُقَدِ). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 11).

غ.#.#.why: غَيّ: the lexicon glosses it as 'transgression; offense'. In the Quran it is error, going astray, the opposite of right guidance (2:256 قَدْ تَبَيَّنَ الرُّشْدُ مِنَ الْغَيِّ). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 11).

ك.ر.ب.why: كَرْب: the lexicon glosses it as 'worries; fears'. In the Quran it is distress, great affliction (21:76 مِنَ الْكَرْبِ الْعَظِيمِ). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 11).

ن.س.ك.why: مَنْسَك: the lexicon glosses it only as 'pilgrimage ceremony'. In the Quran it is a rite of worship in general (22:34 وَلِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ جَعَلْنَا مَنْسَكًا; 2:128 مَنَاسِكَنَا). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 11).

ن.ص.ب.why: نَصَب: the lexicon reads the letters only as نَصْب 'setting up'. In the Quran نَصَب is fatigue, weariness (18:62 لَقَدْ لَقِينَا مِنْ سَفَرِنَا هَٰذَا نَصَبًا; 35:35). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 11).

ث.ل.ل.why: ثُلَّة: the lexicon glosses it as 'troop; detachment'. In the Quran it is a large group of people, a crowd (56:13 ثُلَّةٌ مِنَ الْأَوَّلِينَ). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 11).

س.#.د.why: سَيِّد: the lexicon glosses only the title 'Mr.'; in the Quran it is a master or chief (12:25 سَيِّدَهَا, 33:67 سَادَتَنَا). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 12).

س.ح.ت.why: سُحْت: the lexicon glosses it 'illegal possession'; in the Quran it is unlawful gain (5:42 أَكَّالُونَ لِلسُّحْتِ). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 12).

ف.ج.ج.why: فَجّ: the lexicon glosses only 'road'; in the Quran it is a wide path between mountains (21:31 فِجَاجًا سُبُلًا, 22:27 كُلِّ فَجٍّ عَمِيقٍ). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 12).

ق.ع.د.why: قَوَاعِد: the lexicon glosses 'bases; rules'; of a building they are its foundations (2:127 الْقَوَاعِدَ مِنَ الْبَيْتِ). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 12).

ص.ل.#.why: مُصَلِّين: the lexicon glosses 'people praying'; the plain English is worshippers (70:22 إِلَّا الْمُصَلِّينَ). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 12).

ن.ف.ق.why: نِفَاق: the lexicon reads it as إِنْفَاق 'expenditure'; in the Quran and in MSA it is hypocrisy (9:77 نِفَاقًا فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 12).

ق.س.م.why: قِسْمَة: the lexicon glosses the bare noun only 'allotment; apportionment' (and 'division' only with a possessive); in the Quran it is the division of a share or inheritance (4:8 وَإِذَا حَضَرَ الْقِسْمَةَ, 53:22 قِسْمَةٌ ضِيزَى). Added 2026-11-06 (noun batch 12).
